qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global express hub-and-spoke air network (Memphis World Hub, 680+ aircraft) and sorting infrastructure are virtually impossible to replicate from scratch, but fails empirical proof of moat. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~7.5% (10-year avg ~9.5%), persistently below the 12% quality hurdle across all cycle stages. Pricing power is constrained by UPS, Amazon logistics insourcing/expansion, regional parcel carriers, and belly-cargo substitution; lost the major USPS air cargo contract to UPS in 2024.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). While FedEx operates an irreplaceable global air express and ground logistics network, heavy capital intensity ($4B-$6B+ annual capex for aircraft, hubs, and vehicle fleet) and competitive pressure from UPS and Amazon keep operating margins at 5.5-7.0% and multi-cycle ROIC at 7-8%, well below the 12% threshold.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 7.5% (FY20 4.3%, FY21 10.2%, FY22 8.5%, FY23 7.4%, FY24 7.5%, FY25 ~7.0%), consistently failing the 12% hurdle even during peak pandemic package volume surges. Operating margins oscillate between 5.5% and 7.0%. Ongoing capital intensity ($4.1B capex in FY25, $5.2B in FY24) dampens returns on capital. Pricing power is limited against UPS and Amazon, underscored by the loss of the foundational USPS domestic air cargo contract in 2024.
